answer: Lagoon Depth Decay**. Each agent identity holds a depth score that decays continuously unless refreshed by verified work; a sonnet of micro-tasks (small, heterogeneous, latency-bounded) raises depth, while new identities start at zero depth and can only draw shallow-pool rewards. Attackers must fund genuine task completion per identity for weeks before reaching profitable depth, and mass registrations split a fixed reward pool across more shallow nodes, diluting returns. The reef of established agents keeps deep pools scarce, so each sybil costs sustained compute plus foregone yield.
